newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends steady but backwardation narrows.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends steady but backwardation narrows.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended steady on Tuesday but the backwardation in the swaps market narrowed due to ample prompt availability, brokers said.
March swaps slipped about 75 cents to $205.25/$206.

Firmer crude oil futures and buying by Far East players boosted April swaps, which rose $3.50 to $201.50/$202.50 a tonne and tightened the March/April backwardation to about $3.50, from close to $8 on Monday.

"The April went up because of the crude and the March was hurt because of the prompt pressure on the physical market," a broker said. "Buying April swaps here and selling May in the Far East -- there is an element of that too."
Another broker said the April/May backwardation widened out slightly due to refiner selling in May.

NWE cargoes were notionally down $1 at $203/$207 cif a tonne. An offer was heard early in the afternoon at $205 for pipeline spec material, but that was believed to have been withdrawn when Brent crude jumped nearly 60 cents a barrel by late in the session.
